description: Machine-readable record of what has actually been observed to work, as of the evidence cited per entry -- not a claim about what should work. status values: verified (real cluster/host, evidence cited), build-verified (compiles and passes stubbed-runner unit tests only, no real filesystem/cluster exercised), unverified (implemented, never exercised), known-gap (a specific, named blocker exists).

filesystemBackends.evidence: Air-Gap E2E workflow (.github/workflows/e2e-airgap.yaml): real prjquota-mounted XFS loopback host, quota apply/rolling-upgrade/idempotent-resync and NFSv4 wire-path write rejection verified in CI (#149).

filesystemBackends.evidence: nfs-quota-agent#4 E2E session: unit tests pass (stubbed CommandRunner), but a real ext4 prjquota mount attempt failed with a kernel error ("Failed to enable quota tracking (type=2, err=-3, ino=12)") even after e2fsck -fy on the test host; root cause not diagnosed, session moved to XFS instead.
filesystemBackends.notes: Not a known code defect in internal/quota/ext4.go -- the failure was at the mkfs/mount layer of the one test host tried. PR #155's first Air-Gap E2E ext4 run (33892085732) surfaced and fixed a real read-back verification bug: repquota -P names a project row by its /etc/projid name whenever one is registered, never '#<id>', which internal/quota/report.go's parser didn't handle. The second run (33894294753) surfaced a filesystem-level (not code) gap instead: ext4 project quota hard limits are not enforced for a writer holding CAP_SYS_RESOURCE (root) -- fs/quota/dquot.c ignore_hardlimit() waives them, and knfsd over an export with no_root_squash performs the write as root -- so the E2E's root-owned test writer silently bypassed the 100 MiB limit. Fixed by making the primary Stage D writer non-root (the realistic tenant case, where the limit correctly applies) and adding a supplementary root-writer step that documents the bypass on ext4 while asserting xfs/btrfs still enforce for root. Move to verified with the passing run id once the ext4 matrix job is green end to end.

filesystemBackends.evidence: Agent Behavior runtime-filesystem-tools check builds the shipped image and verifies the btrfs CLI is present in-container; btrfs CommandRunner unit tests also pass. The previous missing-btrfs-progs container defect was reproduced and repaired in PR #86.
filesystemBackends.notes: The image dependency blocker is resolved, but no real Btrfs filesystem E2E exists yet. The target path must already be a subvolume with `btrfs quota enable` configured by the host/operator before this backend can move to verified. PR #155 adds this backend to the Air-Gap E2E matrix; move to verified with the passing run id once that job is green.

knownLimitations.summary: PodDisruptionBudget against a DaemonSet-managed pod fails closed (blocks all Eviction API disruption) on k3s v1.36.3 due to a k8s core limitation ("daemonsets.apps does not implement the scale subresource"). helm-upgrade-driven rolling replacement is unaffected -- it does not go through the Eviction API.
